title: Evidential uncertainty-aware and dual-view prediction fusion for semi-supervised medical image segmentation

model_family.name: U-Net
model_family.role: Primary segmentation backbone and feature extractor

contributions.implementation_detail: Efficiently fusing predictions from two different views (Linear Classifier and Evidential Prototype Classifier).
contributions.improve_from: Existing methods relying on a single prediction branch for pseudo-label generation

contributions.implementation_detail: Constructing an evidential prototype classifier (EPC) that fuses labeled and unlabeled prototypes, and innovatively transforms the similarity between pixel features and corresponding prototypes directly into evidential support.
contributions.improve_from: Existing prototype-based methods relying solely on labeled data

contributions.improvement: More reliable and holistic guidance for pseudo-label generation
contributions.implementation_detail: Integrating evidential deep learning to jointly assess both epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty, and proposing an improved evidential fusion rule that effectively combines dual-view predictions.
contributions.improve_from: Prevailing uncertainty estimation methods based on Shannon entropy alone

limitations: The transformation requires that the outputs of the Linear Classifier (LC) and the Evidential Prototype Classifier (EPC) be on a comparable scale before evidence conversion.
The underlying scale misalignment between the two prediction sources (unbounded logits vs. bounded cosine similarities) is not fully resolved by the hyper-parameter T_p.

Future work needs to explore more comprehensive calibration methods (e.g., distributional alignment via quantile matching or normalization to a shared statistical scale) to better harmonize predictions from heterogeneous classifiers.
